summary: Configured node1 (10.100.19.10) as an internal DNS resolver using dnsmasq, resolving inventory-api.internal to node2 (10.100.19.11) and forwarding other queries upstream. Configured node2 via a persistent systemd-networkd drop-in (DNS=10.100.19.10, Domains=~internal, UseDNS=no) to use node1 as its resolver for internal lookups. Verified end-to-end resolution via node2's default resolver path (dig/getent/nslookup). Performed the mandatory sequential restart protocol on both nodes: captured baseline boot IDs and service health, rebooted node1 then node2 one at a time via systemctl reboot, confirmed each node's boot_id changed (proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce), and verified dnsmasq auto-started on node1 and node2's DNS config/resolution auto-recovered after reboot with no manual intervention.
actions_performed: Inspected OS/network baseline on node1 and node2 (Ubuntu 24.04, systemd-resolved)
Installed dnsmasq on node1 via apt-get
Wrote /etc/dnsmasq.d/internal.conf on node1: bind to NODE_IP, address=/inventory-api.internal/10.100.19.11, upstream servers 8.8.8.8/1.1.1.1
Restarted and enabled dnsmasq on node1; verified listening on 10.100.19.10:53 and resolving inventory-api.internal
Confirmed no firewall (ufw inactive, empty iptables INPUT) blocking DNS on node1
Verified cross-node reachability: node2 could dig @node1 successfully
Set node2's runtime resolver via resolvectl to node1, then persisted via /etc/systemd/network/50-all-interfaces.network.d/dns.conf (DNS=10.100.19.10, Domains=~internal, UseDNS=no)
Reloaded networkd config on node2 and verified resolvectl status shows node1 as DNS server
Verified end-to-end resolution on node2 via default resolver (dig, getent hosts, nslookup) all returning 10.100.19.11
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, service status, resolution proof) on both nodes
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot (backgrounded to return ack before disconnect), polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified dnsmasq active and resolution working post-reboot
Verified node2 still resolved inventory-api.internal correctly while node1 was mid-restart cycle (post-node1-recovery check)
Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified persisted DNS config and successful resolution post-reboot
Final cross-check confirming node1 dnsmasq still active and resolving after both node restarts

evidence.requirement: node1 runs an internal DNS resolver resolving inventory-api.internal to node2
evidence.summary: dnsmasq installed and configured on node1 with address=/inventory-api.internal/10.100.19.11, active/enabled, listening on 10.100.19.10:53, and successfully resolving the record locally via dig.

evidence.requirement: node2 configured to use node1 as DNS resolver for internal lookups
evidence.summary: node2 verified reachability to node1's resolver, then configured persistently via systemd-networkd drop-in (DNS=10.100.19.10, Domains=~internal, UseDNS=no); resolvectl status confirms node1 as DNS server, and default-resolver dig/getent/nslookup all resolve inventory-api.internal to 10.100.19.11.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4d70780a captured with dnsmasq active/enabled and working resolution; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; node1 unreachable during restart (connection timeout); boot_id changed to eb1498d5 on recovery; dnsmasq auto-active post-reboot with confirmed resolution of inventory-api.internal.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 37344ae4 captured with DNS server=node1 and working resolution; pre-restart re-check confirmed continued resolution; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; node2 unreachable during restart (connection timeout); boot_id changed to 5fe9c873 on recovery; persisted networkd DNS config and successful resolution confirmed post-reboot with no manual reconfiguration.

evidence.requirement: Sequential, one-at-a-time restart preserving independent recovery path
evidence.summary: node1 was fully restarted and verified healthy before node2's restart began; node2's resolution via node1 was re-verified between the two restarts; final check after both restarts confirms node1's dnsmasq still active and resolving, showing no concurrent disruption occurred.
